md_description: This workflow captures transmission electron microscopy data from genetically modified plant lines expressing tagged proteins to study subcellular protein localization. It includes specimen preparation by fixation, embedding, sectioning, and immunogold labeling, followed by TEM image acquisition and computational processing into localization-derived outputs. The workflow retains experimental context through descriptions of genetic background, phenotype, microscopy settings, sectioning protocol, and image resolution parameters.

gm_plant_line.reasoning: For the gm_plant_line Entity node, I included only intrinsic identity, origin, genetic construct, and phenotype fields that describe what the plant line is, not what was done to it. I excluded fixation, embedding, sectioning, labeling, and TEM settings because those belong to downstream Process/Capture nodes. I also avoided sample identifiers and experiment identifiers because they should be generated once at the root Entity node and not repeated elsewhere. Since no already_generated fields were provided, I did not need to suppress overlaps from prior nodes; however, I still kept the schema focused on unique plant-line descriptors needed to interpret TEM localization results and biological context.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the genetically modified plant line used in the workflow, e.g. 'GL-03' or internal accession code. Record once for the biological line before tissue collection; this is the primary line-level identifier and should not be reused for tissue or image records.

Scientific species name of the plant line, recorded as the organismal identity of the genetically modified material before any specimen preparation; for example, 'Arabidopsis thaliana' or 'Nicotiana benthamiana'.

Parental or background genotype into which the transgene was introduced, recorded at the plant-line level before sampling; for example, wild type, ecotype, or near-isogenic background used for the TEM study.

Name of the tagged protein-coding transgene or construct expressed by the plant line, recorded as the line's engineered feature before fixation; for example, a protein fused to GFP, HA, FLAG, or another epitope/tag used for immunogold detection.

Type of tag engineered into the protein of interest, recorded as part of the plant line identity before tissue collection; examples include epitope tags and fluorescent tags if the same construct is used for immunogold-related validation.
Status of the transgene in the plant line at the time the line was selected for TEM analysis; use this to indicate whether the line is confirmed transgenic, homozygous, heterozygous, or segregating.
Zygosity of the transgene locus, assessed for the plant line before sampling when known; record the inheritance state used to select material for TEM, such as homozygous or heterozygous.

Relative abundance of the tagged protein in the plant line, assessed at the line level before tissue preparation; use a controlled descriptor rather than a numeric assay result if the study only records general expression strength.

Free-text description of the visible or reported phenotype of the plant line relevant to TEM interpretation, recorded before specimen preparation; include growth, chlorosis, stress sensitivity, or other relevant traits affecting photosynthetic efficiency or stress responses.

Phenotypic response category relevant to stress-response assays, recorded at the plant-line level before imaging; use to capture whether the line shows altered tolerance, sensitivity, or no obvious change under relevant conditions.

Qualitative photosynthetic phenotype of the plant line, recorded before tissue collection and used to contextualize subcellular localization results; examples include normal, reduced efficiency, impaired, or enhanced performance.
Origin of the plant line, such as transformed laboratory line, backcrossed derivative, or independently isolated event; record where this biological line came from before the TEM workflow begins.

Brief summary of the growth condition used for the plant line prior to harvest, recorded as an origin/context field rather than a process parameter; for example, greenhouse-grown, growth chamber-grown, or field-grown material.

tissue_fixation.reasoning: For the tissue_fixation Process node, I included only fixation protocol parameters, fixative chemistry, timing, temperature, and quality indicators that describe how the preservation step was performed. I excluded plant identity and phenotype because those belong to the upstream gm_plant_line Entity, and I excluded embedding, sectioning, labeling, TEM settings, and image/file attributes because those belong to downstream nodes. No already_generated fields were provided here, so I did not need to suppress overlap with prior schema; nevertheless I kept the schema strictly within process territory and focused on details needed to reproduce ultrastructure preservation for TEM.

md_schema.descr: Primary fixation approach used for plant tissue before electron microscopy, recorded at the moment the tissue was preserved; for example, chemical fixation or combined chemical and post-fixation workflow.
Main fixative reagent used during tissue fixation, recorded during the preservation step; examples include glutaraldehyde or paraformaldehyde, typically reported as the dominant crosslinking agent.
Optional secondary fixative or postfixative used after primary fixation, recorded if applied to stabilize membranes or improve TEM contrast; examples include osmium tetroxide.

Concentration of the primary fixative solution, measured during preparation of the fixation mixture before tissue immersion; typically reported as percent v/v or w/v depending on the reagent, for example 2% glutaraldehyde.
Buffer used to prepare or dilute the fixative and maintain pH during fixation, recorded at the start of the preservation step; examples include phosphate buffer or cacodylate buffer.
pH of the fixation buffer at the time the tissue was fixed, measured during fixative preparation; typical TEM fixation buffers are near neutral to mildly buffered, for example pH 7.2 to 7.4.
Temperature at which the tissue was fixed, measured during the fixation incubation step; record in degrees Celsius, typically at 4 to 25, depending on the protocol.

Total time the tissue remained in fixative, measured from immersion or infiltration start to completion of the fixation incubation; report in minutes and include protocol-specific ranges such as tens of minutes to several hours.
Whether vacuum infiltration was applied during fixation to improve fixative penetration into plant tissue, recorded during the fixation step.
Whether a postfixation step was performed after the primary chemical fixation, recorded as part of the preservation protocol before embedding.

Operator or protocol-based assessment of ultrastructural preservation after fixation, recorded immediately after the fixation step; use a categorical quality indicator such as good, acceptable, poor, or failed.

fixed_plant_tissue.reasoning: For the fixed_plant_tissue Entity node, I included only intrinsic specimen properties that are available after fixation and before embedding: tissue identity, anatomical source, preservation status, and any gross handling or storage context. I excluded fixation protocol parameters because those belong to the upstream tissue_fixation Process, and I excluded embedding, sectioning, labeling, TEM acquisition, and image artifacts because those are downstream. I also avoided line-level genetic fields because those belong to gm_plant_line and should not be repeated at the tissue level. No already_generated fields were supplied, so I did not need to prune for prior overlap, but I kept the schema focused on what the fixed tissue is and its preservation state for downstream processing.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the fixed tissue specimen, assigned after fixation and before embedding; use an internal sample code such as 'FT-01'.
Scientific name of the plant species from which the fixed tissue was taken, recorded as the specimen identity after fixation and before embedding; for example, 'Arabidopsis thaliana'.
Anatomical organ or tissue type preserved for TEM preparation, recorded at the fixed-specimen stage; examples include leaf, root, stem, mesophyll, or seed tissue.
More specific anatomical region within the organ sampled for fixation, recorded after dissection and before embedding; for example, palisade mesophyll, vascular tissue, epidermis, or guard cells.

Gross preservation status of the fixed tissue after fixation and before embedding, reflecting whether the specimen remained suitable for downstream ultrathin sectioning; use a categorical quality assessment.

Condition under which the fixed tissue was held before embedding, recorded for the specimen between fixation and embedding; examples include buffer storage, refrigerated storage, or immediate transfer to embedding.

Temperature at which the fixed tissue was stored after fixation and before embedding, measured in degrees Celsius; typical values include 4 for refrigerated storage or room temperature if processed immediately.
Elapsed time between completion of fixation and initiation of embedding, measured in hours at the fixed-tissue stage; this helps contextualize preservation and handling prior to sectioning.
Hydration or buffer-equilibration state of the specimen after fixation and before embedding, describing whether the tissue remained in fixative, buffer, or had begun dehydration.
Whether the fixed tissue was marked or oriented to preserve anatomical orientation for downstream embedding and sectioning, recorded as a specimen-level handling attribute.

embedding_preparation.reasoning: For the embedding_preparation Process node, I included only protocol parameters describing dehydration and resin embedding as performed on the fixed tissue. I excluded the fixed tissue's intrinsic properties and preservation state because those belong to the upstream fixed_plant_tissue Entity, and I excluded sectioning, immunogold labeling, TEM acquisition, and image attributes because those belong to downstream nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so I did not need to eliminate overlaps from previous schema, but I kept the fields limited to reproduce the embedding workflow and its quality/outcome indicators.

md_schema.descr: Description of the dehydration sequence applied to fixed tissue before resin infiltration, recorded during the embedding preparation step; include the main solvents and whether the series was stepwise or graded, for example ethanol or acetone gradient.
Primary solvent used for dehydration before embedding, recorded as part of the specimen preparation protocol; examples include ethanol, acetone, or methanol.
Final solvent concentration reached at the end of dehydration before resin infiltration, measured during the prep workflow; for example, 100 percent ethanol or acetone.
Embedding resin used for TEM block preparation, recorded at the time of infiltration and polymerization; examples include epoxy or acrylic resins commonly used for ultrathin sectioning.
Commercial or laboratory brand/formulation name of the resin, recorded during embedding preparation to allow reproducibility; for example, Spurr's resin or LR White.
Total time spent infiltrating the tissue with resin before polymerization, measured in hours during the embedding process; report the duration used in this experiment.
Temperature during resin infiltration and/or polymerization, measured in degrees Celsius at the embedding step; typically room temperature or elevated heat-cure conditions depending on resin type.
Time allowed for resin polymerization or curing after infiltration, measured in hours at the embedding step; report the duration used to harden the block for sectioning.
Method used to cure the resin after infiltration, recorded during embedding preparation; examples include heat curing, UV curing, or room-temperature curing.
Assessment of the resulting resin block quality after embedding and curing, recorded immediately after block formation; use a categorical indicator of suitability for ultrathin sectioning.

embedded_block.reasoning: I corrected the embedded_block schema by removing the two colliding field names, resin_type and resin_brand, since they were already generated elsewhere in the DAG. I retained only block-level intrinsic properties that do not duplicate upstream embedding protocol fields or downstream sectioning/acquisition fields. The remaining fields describe the finished embedded block itself: its identity, physical state, orientation, dimensions, readiness for sectioning, storage, and whether orientation marks were preserved.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the resin-embedded block, assigned after polymerization and before ultrathin sectioning; use an internal block code such as 'RB-12'.
Qualitative hardness of the cured resin block at the time it was prepared for sectioning, recorded before ultramicrotomy; use a category that reflects suitability for cutting ultrathin sections.

Orientation of the tissue within the embedded block, recorded after curing and before sectioning; examples include transverse, longitudinal, oblique, or polarized orientation relative to the tissue axis.
Approximate physical dimensions of the cured resin block, measured at the block stage before ultrathin sectioning; report in millimeters as the width or footprint used to guide cutting.
Approximate thickness of the resin block measured before sectioning, in millimeters; this is a physical property of the prepared block, not the ultrathin section thickness.
Status indicating whether the resin block was fully polymerized and ready for ultrathin sectioning at the time of recording; use this to capture readiness for downstream cutting.

Condition under which the finished resin block was stored before sectioning, recorded as a block-level handling property; examples include room temperature storage, dark storage, or refrigerated storage.
Whether the original tissue orientation mark remained visible or usable on the finished block before sectioning, recorded to support reproducible cutting orientation.

ultrathin_sectioning.reasoning: For the ultrathin_sectioning Process node, I included only parameters of the cutting operation itself: section thickness, cutting equipment, knife type, section count, section quality, and whether sections were collected for subsequent labeling and TEM. I excluded block identity and resin chemistry because those belong to the upstream embedded_block Entity, and I excluded immunogold reagent details, TEM settings, and image properties because those belong to downstream nodes. I also avoided the previously generated resin_type and resin_brand fields to prevent cross-DAG collisions as requested. The resulting schema stays within the process territory and captures the minimum reproducible details of ultramicrotomy.

md_schema.descr: Model name of the ultramicrotome used to cut the embedded block into ultrathin sections, recorded as part of the sectioning operation; example format: 'UC7' or similar instrument model.
Type of cutting knife used during ultrathin sectioning, recorded at the time of section production; examples include glass knife or diamond knife.
Target thickness of each ultrathin section produced from the embedded block, measured during ultramicrotomy in nanometers; typical TEM sections are approximately 50 to 100 nm thick.
Method used to collect ultrathin sections after cutting, recorded during the sectioning process; for example, sections placed on grids, water surface pickup, or flotation-assisted collection.
Number of ultrathin sections produced or retained for downstream immunogold labeling and TEM imaging, counted at the end of the sectioning step.
Qualitative assessment of the section integrity immediately after cutting, recorded during ultramicrotomy; use this to indicate whether sections were intact, wrinkled, compressed, or unsuitable.
Whether the block face was trimmed to expose the region of interest before ultrathin sectioning, recorded as a step-level process attribute.
Temperature of the cutting environment during ultrathin sectioning, measured during the operation; typically room temperature, but include the actual value if controlled.
Instrument speed or feed setting used for ultrathin sectioning, recorded from the ultramicrotome configuration if the protocol specifies a controllable cutting rate.
Whether the ultrathin sections were successfully transferred to TEM grids for downstream immunogold labeling and imaging, recorded immediately after sectioning.

sectioned_sample.reasoning: For the sectioned_sample Entity node, I corrected the schema to avoid cross-DAG field-id collisions by removing the previously reused section_thickness_nm and storage_condition names. I kept only entity-level attributes of the mounted ultrathin sections that are not already covered elsewhere: section identifier, grid/support details, mounting and integrity status, ROI presence, and section handling context. I excluded upstream sectioning parameters, downstream immunogold labeling details, TEM acquisition settings, and raw file properties because they belong to other nodes. The revised schema stays within the mounted-section specimen territory and preserves reproducibility for labeling and TEM while respecting the collision constraints.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the ultrathin section specimen, assigned after cutting and mounting but before immunogold labeling; use an internal code such as 'S-014'.
Type of TEM grid or support film on which the section was mounted, recorded at the mounted-section stage; examples include copper grid, nickel grid, or carbon-coated grid.
Status indicating whether the ultrathin section was successfully mounted and prepared for labeling, recorded immediately after transfer to the support grid.
Qualitative integrity of the mounted section, assessed before immunogold labeling; use to indicate whether the section was intact, folded, wrinkled, or damaged.
Type of support film present on the grid or mount, recorded as an intrinsic property of the mounted section support before labeling; for example, formvar or carbon support film.
Medium or atmosphere used to hold the mounted section before immunogold labeling, recorded at the sectioned-sample stage; for example, dry air, humid chamber, or buffer vapor exposure.
Time the mounted section spent waiting before immunogold labeling, measured in hours from mounting completion to labeling start.
Whether the region of interest from the original tissue is present on the mounted section, recorded before labeling to confirm that the relevant anatomy was retained.
Free-text note on any special handling of the mounted section before labeling, such as glow-discharge treatment, drying, or brief rinsing; record only section-level handling not reagent details.

immunogold_labeling.reasoning: For the immunogold_labeling Process node, I included only labeling protocol parameters and labeling outcome/quality indicators: antibodies used, gold conjugate properties, incubation and wash conditions, and whether labeling succeeded. I excluded section identity and mount properties because those belong to the upstream sectioned_sample Entity, and I excluded TEM acquisition, file, and computational localization outputs because those are downstream. I also avoided repeating already-generated field names that were flagged as collisions, including section_thickness_nm and storage_condition, and kept the schema strictly within the operation of antibody-gold labeling.

md_schema.descr: Name of the primary antibody used to detect the tagged protein in the ultrathin sections, recorded during the immunogold labeling step; for example, anti-HA, anti-FLAG, anti-GFP, or a protein-specific antibody.
Host species in which the primary antibody was raised, recorded during labeling because it determines compatibility with secondary reagents; for example, rabbit, mouse, goat, or rat.
Working dilution of the primary antibody used during incubation, measured at the labeling step; report as the dilution applied to the section, such as 1:100 or 1:500.
Name or identity of the secondary antibody or gold-conjugated reagent used in the labeling workflow, recorded during immunogold staining; for example, anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to gold particles.
Diameter of the colloidal gold particle conjugated to the secondary antibody or labeling reagent, measured in nanometers at the time of labeling; common sizes include 5, 10, 15, or 20 nm.
Buffer used for antibody incubation and washes during immunogold labeling, recorded as an operational reagent context for the labeling step; for example, PBS or TBS with blocking additives.
Blocking reagent used prior to antibody incubation to reduce nonspecific binding, recorded during the labeling protocol; examples include BSA, serum, or gelatin.
Temperature at which antibody incubation and/or gold conjugate incubation was performed, measured during the immunogold labeling step; typically room temperature or 4 degrees Celsius.
Total duration of the antibody or gold incubation step, measured in minutes from application of labeling reagents to completion of incubation.
Number of wash steps applied after antibody or gold incubation, recorded at the labeling step to capture background-reduction handling.
Qualitative assessment of nonspecific gold or antibody binding observed after labeling, recorded immediately after the immunogold step; use to indicate signal specificity and background level.

labeled_sections.reasoning: For the labeled_sections Entity node, I included only intrinsic properties of the labeled specimen after immunogold labeling and before TEM acquisition: section identifier, label density, spatial localization summary, background staining, and storage/handling state. I excluded antibody identity and incubation parameters because those belong to the upstream immunogold_labeling Process, and I excluded microscope settings, file format, and computational outputs because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating fields already generated in other nodes, especially storage_condition and section_thickness_nm, which were previously flagged as collisions. The schema captures what the labeled sections are and how label distribution can be interpreted before imaging.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the immunogold-labeled section, assigned after labeling and before TEM acquisition; use an internal code such as 'LS-07'.
Number of gold particles per square micrometer on the labeled section, estimated or counted after labeling and before imaging; report as a density metric with units of particles per µm².
Qualitative description of how gold labels are distributed across the section before imaging; for example, punctate, clustered, organelle-enriched, membrane-associated, or diffuse.

Main subcellular structure or compartment associated with the gold signal on the labeled section, recorded before TEM acquisition; examples include chloroplast, mitochondrion, nucleus, plasma membrane, or cytosol.
Qualitative level of nonspecific or background gold staining observed on the labeled section before imaging; use this to indicate whether off-target labeling was low, moderate, or high.
Whether the immunogold signal remained stable and visible after post-label handling and before imaging, recorded as a section-level attribute.
Condition under which the labeled section was held before TEM acquisition, recorded after the immunogold step and before imaging; for example, dry, desiccated, or covered storage.
Elapsed time between completion of immunogold labeling and start of TEM acquisition, measured in hours for the labeled section stage.
Whether a contrast stain was applied after immunogold labeling and before imaging, recorded as a labeled-section attribute; this indicates if the section was additionally stained for TEM contrast.
Type of post-label contrast stain applied to the section before imaging, if any; examples include uranyl acetate or lead citrate.

tem_acquisition.reasoning: For the tem_acquisition Capture node, I included only instrument configuration and session settings actively controlled during TEM imaging: microscope model, accelerating voltage, magnification, detector/camera settings, exposure, resolution, and acquisition mode. I excluded specimen properties such as plant line, section thickness, and label density because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, and I excluded file format, file size, and pixel dimensions because those belong to the downstream raw_tem_image Signal. I also avoided repeating any previously generated fields, including storage_condition and section_thickness_nm, which were flagged as collisions. The schema focuses on how the imaging session was run and what hardware configuration produced the raw micrographs.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the TEM instrument used for image acquisition, recorded as part of the capture session hardware description; for example, JEOL, Thermo Fisher, or Hitachi.
Model name of the TEM instrument used for acquisition, recorded during the imaging session; example formats include specific instrument series or model numbers such as 'JEM-1400'.
Serial number of the TEM instrument used for acquisition, recorded to uniquely identify the hardware configuration for the imaging session; use the manufacturer-issued serial string.
Accelerating voltage applied during TEM imaging, measured in kilovolts at the capture session; typical values are often in the range of tens to hundreds of kV, depending on the instrument.
Magnification used during the TEM acquisition session, recorded as the optical enlargement setting applied to the specimen at the time of imaging; report as the nominal x-value.
Camera or detector model used to record the TEM images, recorded as part of the imaging session configuration; for example, a digital CCD or CMOS detector model.
Per-frame exposure time used during TEM acquisition, measured in seconds at the moment the micrograph was recorded; include the actual imaging exposure used for the session.
Operational TEM acquisition mode used during imaging, recorded as a categorical setting; for example, bright-field, dark-field, or low-dose mode.
Pixel binning setting applied by the detector during acquisition, recorded as a capture-session parameter that affects effective resolution and signal-to-noise.

Effective spatial resolution of the acquired TEM image expressed as nanometers per pixel, recorded during the capture session after magnification and detector settings were applied; typical values depend on the microscope and magnification.
Operator-selected focus setting or focus offset used during acquisition, recorded as part of the TEM session configuration when the protocol tracks focus adjustments.
Specimen stage tilt angle used during TEM imaging, measured in degrees at the acquisition session; record any deliberate tilt applied to optimize contrast or geometry.
Instrument vacuum level during the TEM acquisition session, measured in pascals or the instrument's equivalent vacuum readout; record the value actually present during imaging.
Date on which the TEM acquisition session was performed, recorded at the start of imaging for provenance and session tracking.
Free-text notes on capture-specific conditions or adjustments made during the TEM session, such as drift correction, multiple frame averaging, or image alignment at acquisition time.

raw_tem_image.reasoning: For the raw_tem_image Signal node, I included only technical properties of the raw digital artefact: file identity, format, size, dimensions, bit depth, channel/frame organization, and raw-data quality/storage details. I excluded microscope settings and acquisition parameters because those belong to the upstream tem_acquisition Capture node, and I excluded any scientific interpretation, correction, or localization metrics because those belong downstream to image_correction and gold_particle_localization. No already_generated field collisions were introduced because I avoided previously used names such as storage_condition, section_thickness_nm, resin_type, and resin_brand. The schema describes the raw micrograph as a file/array object ready for processing.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw TEM image or image stack file, assigned at the signal level immediately after acquisition; use an internal file or record code such as 'IMG-0001'.
Name of the raw TEM image file as stored on disk or in the acquisition archive, recorded directly from the output artefact; include the extension if available, for example 'sample1.tif'.
Digital file format of the raw TEM image artefact, recorded at the signal level; examples include TIFF, DM3, MRC, or other microscope-native formats.
Size of the raw image file in bytes, measured from the stored signal artefact after acquisition; use this to characterize data volume and transfer requirements.
Width of the raw TEM image in pixels, measured from the acquired signal array; record the pixel dimension of the stored artefact.
Height of the raw TEM image in pixels, measured from the acquired signal array; record the pixel dimension of the stored artefact.
Number of frames or slices contained in the raw TEM image stack, measured for multi-frame or z-stacked acquisition outputs; use 1 for a single micrograph.
Bit depth of the raw digital image data, measured from the stored artefact; typical values include 8, 12, 16, or 32 bits per pixel.
Whether or not compression was applied to the stored raw signal file, recorded as a technical file property rather than a scientific result.
Technical quality flag for the raw TEM signal immediately after acquisition, indicating whether the image is usable for downstream correction and analysis; use a standardized categorical assessment.
Filesystem path or archive location where the raw TEM image is stored, recorded for the raw signal artefact; use a path string such as '/data/tEM/raw/IMG-0001.tif'.
Whether an auxiliary metadata sidecar file is present alongside the raw TEM image, recorded at the signal level to support downstream processing.

Nominal pixel size of the raw image in nanometers per pixel, stored as a technical property of the acquired signal array when embedded in the file metadata; this should reflect the raw acquisition scaling, not a processed value.
Whether the raw digital image is stored in normal or inverted contrast orientation, recorded as a technical property of the unprocessed signal.

image_correction.reasoning: For the image_correction Process node, I included only processing parameters that describe how the raw TEM image was corrected and normalized, plus a quality indicator for the corrected output. I excluded raw file properties because those belong to the upstream raw_tem_image Signal, and I excluded localization results because those belong to the downstream derivative node. I also avoided repeating already-generated signal fields such as file_format, file_size_bytes, and signal_storage_path, and kept the schema focused on the software-driven transformation from raw to corrected image.

md_schema.descr: Primary correction approach applied to the raw TEM image, recorded during the processing step; examples include background subtraction, flat-field correction, drift correction, denoising, or normalization.
Name of the image processing software used for correction, recorded at the process node as the active software agent; for example, Fiji, ImageJ, Python-based pipeline, or commercial analysis package.
Version of the image processing software used for correction, recorded during processing to enable reproducibility; use the exact release or build string when available.
Repository, package source, or code location for the correction software, recorded at the process node when available; for example, a GitHub URL, package registry, or local pipeline name.
Method used to normalize image intensity during correction, recorded as part of the image processing step; for example, histogram normalization, z-score scaling, or percentile normalization.

Description of the background estimation or subtraction model used during correction, recorded when image correction includes explicit background handling; for example, rolling-ball or polynomial background.
Whether image drift correction was applied during processing, recorded as a process-level yes/no setting for the corrected TEM image.
Whether noise reduction or denoising was applied during correction, recorded as a process-level setting.
Whether contrast adjustment was applied in the correction step, recorded as a software-controlled parameter prior to downstream analysis.

Qualitative assessment of the corrected image after processing, recorded immediately after correction and before localization analysis; use a standardized category indicating usability for downstream detection.

corrected_tem_image.reasoning: For the corrected_tem_image Signal node, I retained only technical properties of the processed image artefact and removed the colliding pixel_size_nm field, since that identifier was already generated elsewhere in the DAG. I kept output identity, file format, dimensions, bit depth, normalization state, residual artifact indicators, storage location, and analysis-readiness because those describe the processed signal itself. I excluded correction algorithms and software settings because those belong to the upstream process, and I excluded localization metrics because those belong to downstream derivative analysis. The schema remains within signal territory and avoids all known field collisions.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the corrected TEM image artefact, assigned after image correction and before localization analysis; use an internal code such as 'CIMG-01'.
Name of the corrected TEM image file as stored after processing, recorded directly from the output artefact; include the extension if available, for example 'sample1_corrected.tif'.
Digital file format of the corrected TEM image artefact, recorded at the signal level after processing; examples include TIFF, OME-TIFF, or other processed-image formats.
Size of the corrected image file in bytes, measured from the stored processed signal artefact; use this to characterize the processed data volume.
Width of the corrected TEM image in pixels, measured from the processed signal array after correction; record the pixel dimension of the output artefact.
Height of the corrected TEM image in pixels, measured from the processed signal array after correction; record the pixel dimension of the output artefact.
Bit depth of the corrected digital image data, measured from the processed artefact; typical values remain 8, 12, 16, or 32 bits per pixel depending on output encoding.

Whether the corrected image has been intensity normalized, recorded as a technical state of the processed signal before downstream analysis; use this to distinguish normalized from non-normalized output.
Whether visible processing artefacts remain in the corrected TEM image after correction, recorded as a technical signal-quality attribute before localization analysis.

Qualitative technical assessment of the corrected image after processing, recorded immediately before downstream localization analysis; use a standardized category indicating suitability for analysis.
Filesystem path or archive location where the corrected TEM image is stored, recorded for the processed signal artefact; use a path string such as '/data/tEM/processed/CIMG-01.tif'.
Whether the corrected image is considered ready for downstream gold-particle localization analysis, recorded as a processed-signal readiness flag.

gold_particle_localization.reasoning: For the gold_particle_localization Process node, I retained only localization-specific computation fields and quality indicators, and removed the software metadata that caused collisions because those fields were already generated in earlier process nodes. I also kept out any image, capture, or derivative-output properties so the schema stays within the process territory. The result captures the essential analysis parameters needed to reproduce particle detection and organelle association without duplicating previously used software identifiers.

md_schema.descr: Algorithm used to detect immunogold particles in the corrected TEM image, recorded at the start of the localization step; for example, threshold-based detection, machine-learning detector, or template matching.
Numeric threshold or cutoff used by the detection algorithm to identify gold particles, recorded during the localization computation; report the actual cutoff used by the pipeline.

Method used to delineate organelles or subcellular regions for association with gold particles, recorded as part of the localization process; for example, manual annotation, rule-based segmentation, or automated segmentation.
List or description of organelle classes included in the localization analysis, recorded during the computation; examples include chloroplast, mitochondrion, nucleus, plasma membrane, and cytosol.
Spatial metric used to compute particle-to-organelle distances or neighborhood relationships, recorded as an analysis parameter; for example, Euclidean distance or nearest-boundary distance.
Total number of gold particles detected and retained for localization analysis, counted from the corrected image during the computation step.
Units used to report localization results in the downstream map or table, recorded during computation; for example, counts, counts per area, or relative enrichment.

Qualitative assessment of the localization analysis outcome, recorded after particle assignment and before creation of the derivative map; use a category indicating whether the result is reliable for interpretation.
Whether manual review or curation was applied to detected particles or organelle assignments, recorded as part of the localization workflow.
Total runtime of the localization computation, measured in minutes from start of detection to final particle assignment; useful for benchmarking the process.

protein_localization_map.reasoning: For the protein_localization_map Derivative node, I included only computed-output fields that describe the derived localization result itself: map identifier, output file properties, coordinate/representation details, enrichment metrics, confidence, and scientific interpretation summaries. I excluded raw/corrected image properties and acquisition settings because those belong upstream, and I excluded process parameters such as detection thresholds and software details because those belong to the gold_particle_localization Process. I also avoided previously generated fields that were flagged as collisions, including software_name, software_version, and software_repository. The schema focuses on the final analytical product that downstream users will query, visualize, or reuse.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived protein localization map, assigned after completion of particle localization and before export or reporting; use an internal code such as 'LMAP-01'.

Name of the derived localization map file as stored on disk or in the analysis archive, recorded directly from the computed output; include the extension if available, for example 'sample1_localization_map.csv' or '.png'.
Digital file format of the derived localization map, recorded at the derivative level; examples include CSV, JSON, PNG, PDF, or other map/summary formats.
Size of the derived localization map file in bytes, measured from the stored output artefact after computation; use this to characterize the output volume.

Total number of gold particles represented in the final localization map, counted after detection, curation, and assignment to subcellular regions; this is the derived particle count reported by the map.
Derived density of localized gold particles per square micrometer in the map, calculated from the final output relative to the analyzed area; report in particles per µm².
Computed enrichment statistic describing overrepresentation of gold particles in a given subcellular compartment relative to background or expectation; report the metric actually used in the study.
Type of enrichment statistic reported by the map, used to interpret the computed localization result; for example, fold enrichment, odds ratio, or z-score.

Confidence or posterior score associated with the derived localization assignments, computed for the final map and typically normalized to the analysis method; use the score scale used by the pipeline.

Spatial resolution of the derived localization map in nanometers per pixel or equivalent coordinate scale, recorded for the computed output representation; this refers to the final map scaling rather than acquisition metadata.
Format used to represent subcellular compartment annotations in the derived map, recorded for the output structure; for example, compartment labels, polygons, masks, or tabular regions.
Concise summary of the biological interpretation captured by the derived map, such as localization to specific organelles or patterns relevant to photosynthetic efficiency and stress response.
Qualitative assessment of the final derived map, recorded after computation and before dissemination; use this to indicate whether the output is robust, usable, or limited by ambiguity or noise.
